source_metadata.title: Pregnancy and Neonatal Outcomes After Fetal Exposure to Biologics and Thiopurines Among Women With Inflammatory Bowel Disease
authors: Crohn's Colitis Foundation Clinical Research Alliance

atoms.canonical_statement: PIANO assessed pregnancy and infant outcomes after in utero exposure to biologics, thiopurines, or combination therapy in women with inflammatory bowel disease.
PIANO was a prospective, observational, multicenter cohort conducted at 30 US centers between January 2007 and March 2019.
Eligible participants were pregnant women with inflammatory bowel disease and singleton pregnancies.

population.label: Pregnant women with IBD and singleton pregnancies

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants completed questionnaires at intake, each subsequent trimester, delivery, and 4, 9, and 12 months after birth.
Offspring enrolled after 2010 were assessed for developmental milestones at 12, 24, 36, and 48 months after the estimated due date.
Of 1712 enrolled patients, 1490 completed pregnancies and 1431 resulted in live births.
One-year infant outcome measurements were available for 1010 offspring.
The exposure groups included 379 unexposed pregnancies, 242 thiopurine-exposed pregnancies, 642 biologic-exposed pregnancies, and 227 combination-exposed pregnancies.
The cohort included 921 participants with Crohn disease, 535 with ulcerative colitis, and 34 with IBD unclassified.
Among 869 pregnancies exposed to biologic or combination therapy, 51 involved more than one biologic.
Medication exposure was defined as thiopurine or biologic use during the 3 months before the last menstrual period or at any time during pregnancy.

exposures.details: Use in the 3 months before last menstrual period or during pregnancy

atoms.canonical_statement: The unexposed group included pregnancies without biologic or thiopurine exposure; mesalamine, corticosteroids, and antibiotics were permitted in this group.

exposures.details: May include mesalamine, corticosteroids, or antibiotics

atoms.canonical_statement: The biologic exposure group included anti-TNF agents, anti-integrins, and anti-interleukin-12/23 therapy.
The thiopurine exposure group included azathioprine or 6-mercaptopurine.
Combination exposure was defined as biologic plus thiopurine therapy.
Active inflammatory bowel disease was defined as moderate or severe disease activity; remission or mild disease was considered inactive.

outcome.definition: Moderate or severe disease activity by HBI for Crohn disease or SCCAI for ulcerative colitis

atoms.canonical_statement: An IBD flare required an active disease score plus a new medication, prescription change, IBD-related surgery, or IBD-related hospitalization.

outcome.definition: Active HBI/SCCAI plus treatment change, surgery, or hospitalization

atoms.canonical_statement: Preterm birth was defined as delivery before 37 weeks of gestation.
Low birth weight was defined as birth weight below 2500 g.
Serious infant infection was defined as an infection requiring hospitalization; nonserious infection was a reported infection without hospitalization.

outcome.definition: Serious if hospitalization required; nonserious if reported without hospitalization

atoms.canonical_statement: Development was measured with the Ages and Stages Questionnaire, 3rd edition, across communication, fine motor, gross motor, personal-social, and problem-solving domains.
The study primary outcomes were congenital malformations, spontaneous abortion, preterm birth, low birth weight, and infant infections.

outcome.definition: Congenital malformations, spontaneous abortion, preterm birth, low birth weight, and infant infections

atoms.canonical_statement: Pregnancy and neonatal outcomes were compared across exposure groups using crude analyses followed by regression adjusted for relevant maternal, disease, and infant confounders.
Spontaneous abortion analyses were limited to pregnancies enrolled before 20 weeks and used Cox proportional hazards models.
Infant infection models adjusted for preterm birth, maternal age, and disease activity and included sensitivity analyses by biologic class and individual anti-TNF agent.
Developmental milestone scores were compared by drug exposure against the unexposed IBD group and general population means using t tests.
Placental transfer analyses measured maternal, cord, and infant serum concentrations at delivery and used Spearman correlation and Kruskal-Wallis testing for associations with outcomes.
The primary analysis used complete cases because missing data were described as rare.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, biologic therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.2 for any pregnancy complication with a 95% CI of 0.8 to 1.7.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, thiopurine therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.3 for any pregnancy complication with a 95% CI of 0.8 to 2.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 0.8 for any pregnancy complication with a 95% CI of 0.5 to 1.3.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, biologic therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.3 for spontaneous abortion before 140 days with a 95% CI of 0.5 to 3.3.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, thiopurine therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.4 for spontaneous abortion before 140 days with a 95% CI of 0.4 to 4.2.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.2 for spontaneous abortion before 140 days with a 95% CI of 0.4 to 3.8.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, biologic therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 0.9 for preterm birth with a 95% CI of 0.5 to 1.5.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, thiopurine therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.4 for preterm birth with a 95% CI of 0.8 to 2.6.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.8 for preterm birth with a 95% CI of 1 to 3.3.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, biologic therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.1 for small for gestational age with a 95% CI of 0.5 to 2.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, thiopurine therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 0.5 for small for gestational age with a 95% CI of 0.2 to 1.5.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 0.7 for small for gestational age with a 95% CI of 0.3 to 1.8.

Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.2 for low birth weight with a 95% CI of 0.6 to 2.5.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, biologic therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 0.6 for intrauterine growth restriction with a 95% CI of 0.2 to 1.4.

Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 0.7 for intrauterine growth restriction with a 95% CI of 0.2 to 2.3.

Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, thiopurine therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.3 for cesarean section with a 95% CI of 0.9 to 1.9.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.7 for cesarean section with a 95% CI of 1.1 to 2.5.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, biologic therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.1 for nicu admission at birth with a 95% CI of 0.7 to 1.9.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, thiopurine therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.2 for nicu admission at birth with a 95% CI of 0.6 to 2.2.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.5 for nicu admission at birth with a 95% CI of 0.8 to 2.8.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, biologic therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.5 for congenital malformations with a 95% CI of 0.9 to 2.5.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, thiopurine therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.4 for congenital malformations with a 95% CI of 0.8 to 2.7.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.6 for congenital malformations with a 95% CI of 0.8 to 3.1.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, biologic therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.2 for composite excluding cesarean section with a 95% CI of 0.9 to 1.6.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, thiopurine therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.4 for composite excluding cesarean section with a 95% CI of 1 to 2.
Compared with no biologic or thiopurine exposure, combination therapy had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.2 for composite excluding cesarean section with a 95% CI of 0.8 to 1.8.
Congenital malformations were reported in 133 infants, about 9% of the cohort.
Spontaneous abortion occurred in 42 pregnancies, about 3% of completed pregnancies.
Low birth weight occurred in 91 infants, about 7% of reported births.
Preterm birth occurred in 132 pregnancies, about 10% of reported births.
Any infant infection during the first year occurred in 658 of 1431 live births, 46%.
Serious infant infection during the first year occurred in 79 of 1431 live births, 6%.
Biologic therapy was not associated with increased risk of any infant infection in the first year; adjusted OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.20.
Thiopurine therapy was not associated with increased risk of any infant infection in the first year; adjusted OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.28.
Combination therapy was not associated with increased risk of any infant infection in the first year; adjusted OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.32.
Preterm birth was independently associated with infant infection in the first year, adjusted OR 1.73, 95% CI 1.19 to 2.51.
Biologic therapy had a hazard ratio of 1.20 for spontaneous abortion before 20 weeks, with a 95% CI of 0.50 to 2.90.
Thiopurine therapy had a hazard ratio of 0.96 for spontaneous abortion before 20 weeks, with a 95% CI of 0.28 to 3.33.
Combination therapy had a hazard ratio of 0.96 for spontaneous abortion before 20 weeks, with a 95% CI of 0.28 to 3.33.
Active IBD had a hazard ratio of 3.41 for spontaneous abortion before 20 weeks, with a 95% CI of 1.51 to 7.69.
Prior spontaneous abortion had a hazard ratio of 2.17 for spontaneous abortion before 20 weeks, with a 95% CI of 1.05 to 4.49.
At delivery, the median infant serum concentration for Infliximab was 27.1 micrograms/mL in the measured subset.

atoms.canonical_statement: At 12 months, biologic-exposed infants had an ASQ3 communication mean-score difference of 1.9 points versus unexposed infants, p=0.12.
At 12 months, biologic-exposed infants had an ASQ3 fine motor mean-score difference of 0.6 points versus unexposed infants, p=0.46.
At 12 months, biologic-exposed infants had an ASQ3 gross motor mean-score difference of 3.2 points versus unexposed infants, p=0.06.
At 12 months, biologic-exposed infants had an ASQ3 personal-social mean-score difference of 3.5 points versus unexposed infants, p=0.01.
At 12 months, biologic-exposed infants had an ASQ3 problem solving mean-score difference of 2.2 points versus unexposed infants, p=0.1.
Women with ulcerative colitis had lower remission rates by trimester and more flares than women with Crohn disease.
Exposure to more than one biologic was associated with pregnancy flare in 47% versus 20% among those exposed to one biologic, p=0.001.
The supplemental analytic plan states that 202 women enrolled in a subsequent pregnancy and each pregnancy was analyzed as a distinct mother-baby pair.
The supplemental plan allowed enrollment until one day before delivery and later preferential enrollment of therapies of interest after enough unexposed pregnancies had accrued.
The supplemental plan classified Crohn disease activity using HBI thresholds and ulcerative colitis activity using SCCAI thresholds.
The supplemental placental-transfer plan requested repeat infant levels at 3 and 6 months only when the infant level exceeded 2 micrograms/mL.
The supplemental plan notes that assays for biologics other than infliximab and adalimumab used versions that had not undergone complete development and validation at the time of the plan.
Of 1712 enrolled participants, 146 lacked a completed pregnancy outcome after excluding ongoing pregnancies and multiple gestations; 128 were lost to follow-up and 18 withdrew consent.

Post hoc power calculations indicated the observed sample could detect relative risks of about 1.64 for congenital malformations, 2.30 for spontaneous abortion, 1.58 for preterm birth, and 2.00 for small-for-gestational-age birth at 80% power and alpha 0.05.
In adjusted growth analyses at birth, thiopurine therapy had a relative risk of 0.55 for birth weight below 25th percentile versus unexposed pregnancies, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.94, p=0.03.

atoms.canonical_statement: At first trimester, flare was reported in 18% with biologic therapy versus 27% in the unexposed group; the overall group comparison was p=<0.0001.
At first trimester, flare was reported in 13% with thiopurine therapy versus 27% in the unexposed group; the overall group comparison was p=<0.0001.
At first trimester, flare was reported in 15% with combination therapy versus 27% in the unexposed group; the overall group comparison was p=<0.0001.
At third trimester, flare was reported in 7% with biologic therapy versus 12% in the unexposed group; the overall group comparison was p=.003.
At third trimester, flare was reported in 9% with thiopurine therapy versus 12% in the unexposed group; the overall group comparison was p=.003.
At third trimester, flare was reported in 3% with combination therapy versus 12% in the unexposed group; the overall group comparison was p=.003.
At 4 months postpartum, flare was reported in 15% with biologic therapy versus 24% in the unexposed group; the overall group comparison was p=.009.
At 4 months postpartum, flare was reported in 12% with thiopurine therapy versus 24% in the unexposed group; the overall group comparison was p=.009.
At 4 months postpartum, flare was reported in 12% with combination therapy versus 24% in the unexposed group; the overall group comparison was p=.009.
At 24 months, the combination-exposed group had a fine-motor mean-score difference of -3.8 points versus unexposed infants, p=0.02.
At 24 months, the biologic-exposed group had a gross-motor mean-score difference of 2.2 points versus unexposed infants, p=0.03.
At 36 and 48 months, Table S12 did not show statistically significant ASQ3 domain differences between exposed groups and the unexposed group.
Supplemental Table S6 showed no clear recurring pattern of congenital malformation by drug exposure class.
Supplemental Table S7 did not show a clear increase in first-year infant infections for any individual biologic agent, although several newer-biologic groups were small.

The authors concluded that biologic, thiopurine, or combination therapy during pregnancy was not associated with increased adverse maternal or fetal outcomes at birth or during the first year of life.
The authors stated that these therapies can be continued throughout pregnancy in women with IBD to maintain disease control and reduce pregnancy-related adverse events.
The study relied substantially on patient-reported data and lacked objective markers of inflammatory bowel disease activity.
The observational design leaves potential confounding by indication and treatment selection despite adjusted analyses.
Loss to follow-up could introduce selection bias, although the supplement reports similar measured characteristics among completers and those lost or withdrawn.
The cohort was relatively affluent and highly educated, which limits generalizability of developmental findings.
Post hoc power indicates the study was not designed to exclude small increases in rare outcomes such as congenital malformations or spontaneous abortion.
Repeated pregnancies from 202 women were analyzed as distinct mother-baby pairs, and the supplied analysis plan does not describe clustering by mother.
Funding included a Crohn's Colitis Foundation Senior Research Award, the Lisa and Douglas Goldman Foundation, the Lata and Vaibhav Goel Foundation, and NIH P30 DK034987.
The article reports multiple author relationships with pharmaceutical companies and research sponsors; several authors also reported no relevant conflicts.
